title: Param probing and repair playbook for tool/function calls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: callers (LLMs + multimodal agents + third-party SDKs) frequently send malformed or semantically ambiguous parameters when invoking tools/functions. Existing broad validation either rejects useful inputs or returns opaque errors that are hard for app engineers and end users to remediate. We need a standardized JSON-schema definition format and an operational playbook that: 1) probes ambiguous inputs, 2) attempts safe repair/coercion where appropriate, 3) surfaces actionable, localized error hints, and 4) exposes telemetry to quantify failure modes. Goal: reduce tool-call user-visible failures by 50% and developer debugging time by 30% for common parameter classes (dates, enumerations, IDs, nested optional blocks).
success_criteria: 50% drop in tool-call error rate for top-10 call manifests within 6 weeks of rollout
SDKs show consistent human-friendly error messages (same codes/messages across Python/JS/Go)
Observability: heatmap of repair actions + post-repair success metric in Console
No customer-facing behavior changes for existing strict-compat mode unless opted in
design_summary: Introduce a lightweight JSON-schema extension (call-profile) with three orthogonal concepts: 'expectations' (type, enum, pattern, format), 'repairHints' (coercion strategies prioritized with safety tags), and 'diagnosticSnippets' (short, localized descriptions and examples). Validation runs in two passes: pre-serialize static validation (fast, rejects obvious mismatches) and runtime probing/repair (attempts safe transforms with audit trail). We keep strict-compat feature flag to preserve old reject-on-any-invalid behavior for customers that require deterministic failure semantics.
schema_format_notes: We reuse JSON Schema Draft-07 as the base shape but add a small extension namespace 'x:rw' for runtime hints: x:rw.repairHints (list of {strategy, confidence, safeLevel}), x:rw.exampleInputs, x:rw.legacyAliases (strings). Extension rules: validators ignore unknown x:rw fields; SDKs may surface repairHints to developers; runtime honors 'safeLevel' (low/medium/high) when auto-repair is enabled.
validation_flow: 1) Client/SDK-side preliminary lint: quick schema conformance, return client-side error with inline examples. 2) Server-side pre-validate: shallow check for required keys and types. 3) Runtime probe: where pre-validate fails but repairHints exist, runtime attempts deterministic repairs in descending confidence order and emits an event per-action. 4) Final evaluation: if repair succeeds, call proceeds and a 'repairApplied' header is returned; if not, error with enriched diagnostics and remediation suggestions.
error_taxonomy: We define canonical error codes and short messages to be surfaced across SDKs and Console: ERR_PARAM_MISSING: 'required parameter missing', ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH: 'type mismatch', ERR_ENUM_INVALID: 'invalid enum value', ERR_FORMAT_INVALID: 'format invalid', ERR_REPAIR_FAILED: 'attempted repair failed', ERR_AMBIGUOUS: 'ambiguous value, multiple plausible repairs', ERR_UNSUPPORTED_FIELD: 'field not recognized'. Each code maps to a friendly message, a 1-line remediation hint, and a 'developer_hint' example string for diagnostics.
developer_error_examples:
- ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH: sent 'price': 'twenty' -> hint: 'Try numeric string or number; we can coerce quoted numbers.'; repairHint tried: parseFloat -> success -> returned 'repairApplied: price: parseFloat' header.
- ERR_ENUM_INVALID: sent 'region': 'uswest' -> hint: 'Did you mean us-west or us-west-2?'; repairHint tried: fuzzy-match enums -> ambiguous -> returned ERR_AMBIGUOUS with top 3 suggestions.
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit events: call.validate.start, call.validate.result (ok|repaired|failed), call.repair.action (strategy, confidence, safeLevel), call.repair.outcome, call.error.code. Measure: repair rate, post-repair success rate, per-schema failure heatmap, median time spent in repair. Expose Console dashboard tile 'Tool call resilience' and alerts if post-repair success < 75% for a manifest.
sdk_integration_notes: SDKs expose two toggles: 'autoRepair' (opt-in default=false for safety) and 'strictCompat' (for customers that require prior semantics). SDKs should perform client-side linting using the call-profile to give earlier, localized errors. Python/JS SDKs will include a humanizeError() util that maps codes to messages and examples. When repairApplied, SDK includes a structured 'rw_repair' array in response metadata (stringified array is allowed for transport).
compatibility_strategy: Backward compatibility achieved via: 1) strictCompat toggle (default false during rollout), 2) 'x:rw.legacyAliases' to accept historical field names, 3) opt-in feature flags per-customer for autoRepair, and 4) graceful fallback to previous runtime behavior if request header 'x-rw-runtime-version' < 2.0. We will version the call-profile schema with 'profileVersion' and support up-conversion rules in the runtime shim.
rollout_plan: 1) Week 0: land schema parser + telemetry + CI validation. 2) Week 1: opt-in beta for internal teams and 3 pilot customers; SDKs expose autoRepair behind flag. 3) Week 3: gradual rollout to 10% of traffic, monitor metrics and customer feedback. 4) Week 5: 100% rollout with ability to toggle off per-customer. 5) Post-rollout: 4-week observation and iterate on repairHints for top failure modes.
testing_qa: Unit tests for parser, repair strategies, and deterministic outcomes. E2E tests: sample manifests exercising enums, date parsing (multiple locales), nested optional blocks, arrays with mixed types. Fuzz tests using corpus of historical failing calls. Manual: run internal debug harness, collect Console heatmaps, validate SDK humanized messages.
open_decisions: Default for autoRepair: opt-in or opt-out? (proposal: opt-in for public customers, enable for internal).
How verbose should 'repairApplied' header be? (proposal: short code + diff snippet not full rewritten payload).
Should runtime attempt cross-field repairs that infer values (e.g., derive timezone from locale)? (proposal: restrict to single-field repairs in v1)
What retention window for repair telemetry? (proposal: 90 days for heatmaps, 365 for top manifests)
